title: A complete setup commits no secret and no absolute home path
statement: After a complete setup against an environment-authenticated provider and an enabled research connection, every committed file the setup produced or modified is asserted to contain no API key, token, authorisation header, credential-derived fingerprint, or absolute user path - the set taken from what the setup actually wrote, not from a list fixed in advance - and `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are each asserted explicitly by name.
notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138. A complete run against an environment-authenticated provider — asserted from the preflight's own line — with research enabled and its connection checked. THE FILE SET IS WHAT THIS RUN ADDED OR CHANGED: git's own answer before and after, NUL-delimited so a newline in a path cannot read as two entries, with the rename form handled. There is no exemption list: every entry in that set is read, and one that is not a regular file fails. A file the operator writes before the run, carrying a key and a path of its own, is outside the set, which is how the boundary is observable. Every file in it carries no credential, nothing derived from one (sha256 hex and base64, base64 of the key, a prefix), no authorisation header, no path belonging to this machine by value OR BY SHAPE, and not even the names of the credential variables. `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are asserted in that set by name; the ignored consent and compatibility records are asserted not to be. Deleting the assertions fails nothing, because nothing currently leaks, so what proves the scan bites is injected leaks: a credential variable's name in settings, an absolute path in a generated document, and the research key in the project record are each caught, as is widening the set back to the whole after-state.
